cards.front: How often is alcohol involved in fatal crashes, and who does it affect more, new or experienced drivers?
cards.back: Alcohol rides in over forty percent of fatal crashes, any sip lifts crash odds, and green drivers suffer worse than veterans.

cards.front: What does a person risk by driving after drinking?
cards.back: Drinking drivers risk stiff fines, pricier insurance, lost licenses and jail cells.

cards.front: What path does alcohol take through the body, what does it numb first, and what comparison does the manual use?
cards.back: Drink travels stomach to blood to brain, first numbing judgment itself, so overdose announces only past the point of return like late felt sunburn.

cards.front: As the amount of alcohol rises, which driving skills get worse?
cards.back: Rising doses dull reflexes, sight, alertness, distance and speed math, other car tracking, and basic vehicle control.

cards.front: What is the safest advice about drinking and driving, and what is different for drivers under twenty one?
cards.back: Safest counsel is never drive after drinking, since any dose can impair and arrest, and under twenty one a single drink may suffice.

cards.front: What counts as one drink, and what about exotic mixed drinks?
cards.back: One drink means a shot and a half of eighty proof liquor, a regular twelve ounce beer, or a five ounce wine, while exotic mixes can pack several.

cards.front: Which servings each count as one drink, and how can fancy mixed drinks differ?
cards.back: A shot and a half of liquor, a regular beer, or a five ounce wine each count one drink, while fancy mixed drinks can secretly equal several.

cards.front: Which so called sobering tricks never work, and what is the only thing that does?
cards.back: Coffee, air, exercise and cold showers never hurry sobriety; only passing time does.

cards.front: Can coffee, fresh air, workouts or cold showers speed sobriety, and what clears alcohol from the body?
cards.back: Coffee, fresh air, workouts and cold showers never speed sobriety; only elapsed time clears alcohol from the body.

cards.front: What are the smart ways to get home from a party where people drink?
cards.back: Party smart by rotating a dry designated driver among two plus friends, or by riding transit and cabs home.

cards.front: Which common medicines can affect driving, and how?
cards.back: Headache, cold, allergy and nerve pills, prescription or store bought, can sedate and warp reflexes, judgment, vision and alertness like liquor or worse.

cards.front: What should a driver do before taking a medicine, and why never combine it with alcohol?
cards.back: Read every drug label for driving warnings, quiz doctors or druggists when unsure, and never mix pills with alcohol lest effects multiply toward sickness or death.

cards.front: How do cold, headache, allergy and nerve medicines act alone, and what happens when they are stacked with liquor?
cards.back: Cold, headache, allergy and nerve medicines alone mimic liquor behind the wheel, and stacked with liquor they multiply toward grave illness or death.

cards.front: Who imposes drunk driving penalties, which tests can be asked for, and what does failing cost?
cards.back: Drunk driving draws court plus Commissioner penalties: a blood, breath or urine test, then on failure at least forty five suspended days plus an ignition interlock for six months minimum, longer with priors.

cards.front: What does refusing every test cost, and does age matter?
cards.back: Refusing every test at any age still costs forty five days plus a year minimum interlock, stretching with priors.

cards.front: How does the interlock time differ between failing the chemical test and refusing every test?
cards.back: Failing the chemical test costs forty five days plus six interlock months, while refusing every test costs forty five days plus a full interlock year.

cards.front: What does zero tolerance mean for drivers under twenty one, where does it apply, and what does failure cost?
cards.back: Under twenty one zero tolerance treats any measurable drink, two hundredths percent and up on roads or private land, as arrestable, with failure costing forty five days and a year minimum interlock.

cards.front: At what level does zero tolerance apply to drivers under twenty one, and does it cover private lots?
cards.back: Drivers under twenty one face zero tolerance at two hundredths percent on public roads and private lots alike, with failures drawing forty five days and a year minimum interlock.

cards.front: Which teen convictions suspend the license or licensing privileges of sixteen and seventeen year olds?
cards.back: Teen convictions for restriction breaks, speeding, reckless driving, street racing or phone use all suspend sixteen and seventeen year old licenses or licensing privileges.

cards.front: What do first and later teen restriction breaks cost?
cards.back: First restriction breaks cost thirty days plus a hundred seventy five dollar restoration fee and court fines, while later ones cost six months or until eighteen, whichever lasts longer, plus the same money.

cards.front: How long do repeat restriction breaks last?
cards.back: Repeat restriction breaks span six months or stretch to the eighteenth birthday, whichever lasts longer, on top of the per offense ladders.

cards.front: What is the suspension ladder for teen phone and texting tickets?
cards.back: Teen phone and texting tickets ladder thirty days, then ninety, then six months, each plus a hundred seventy five dollar restoration fee and court fines.

cards.front: What is the suspension ladder for teen speeding twenty or more over the limit?
cards.back: Teen speeding twenty plus over ladders sixty days, then ninety, then six months, each plus a hundred seventy five dollar restoration fee and court fines.

cards.front: How does the teen phone ladder compare with the teen speeding ladder?
cards.back: Teen phone tickets climb thirty, ninety, then one hundred eighty days, while teen twenty over speeding climbs sixty, ninety, then one hundred eighty days.

decks.module: Serious teen offenses and youth status

cards.front: What do first and later teen GDL and reckless driving counts cost?
cards.back: Teen GDL and reckless counts open six months plus fees and fines or up to thirty jail days, then year long suspensions with fines or up to a year locked, second and third times alike.

cards.front: What do first and later teen street racing counts cost?
cards.back: Teen street racing opens six months plus fees and fines or up to a year locked, then year long suspensions with the same money or jail, second and third times alike.

cards.front: How does the first offense jail limit for GDL and reckless counts compare with first street racing counts?
cards.back: First GDL and reckless counts add up to thirty jail days, but first street racing counts add up to a full jail year.

cards.front: Which offenses by drivers under eighteen can never earn youthful offender status?
cards.back: Someone under eighteen cannot be considered a youthful offender for negligent homicide with a motor vehicle, evading responsibility after a crash resulting in death or serious injury, or driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

cards.front: Which youthful offender findings still reach DMV for license suspensions?
cards.back: Youthful findings for reckless, suspended or property flight driving, street racing and officer eluding still reach DMV for license suspensions.

cards.front: Which offenses bar youthful offender status outright, and which ones are only reported to DMV?
cards.back: Under eighteen, negligent homicide with a motor vehicle, evading a crash causing death or serious injury, and DUI of alcohol or drugs bar youthful offender status, whereas youthful offender adjudications for reckless driving, driving under suspension, evading a property-damage or non-serious-injury crash, street racing, or eluding police are disclosed to DMV for suspension.

cards.front: What should you do when a police vehicle with flashing blue lights or a siren stops you?
cards.back: Blue flashing or wailing stops want a right edge park clear of crossings, frozen cabin movement, wheel and visible hands, papers on request only, shut doors, seated waiting and lit domes by night.

cards.front: Where should you fight a ticket you disagree with?
cards.back: Contested tickets get fought in court, never argued roadside with the officer.

cards.front: What does the retraining school teach, and who must attend it?
cards.back: Retraining school teaching operation basics, attitude versus aggression, and safe habits awaits drivers twenty four and under after two moving or suspension counts and older drivers after three.

cards.front: Which teen violations can trigger retraining?
cards.back: Teen retraining triggers include permit breaches, GDL breaches, and any under eighteen phone touching even hands free.

cards.front: What happens after retraining if a driver gets one more moving count within three years?
cards.back: One more moving count within three retrained years suspends the license at least thirty days.

cards.front: How do the retraining triggers differ by age, and what follows a moving count within three years?
cards.back: Drivers age twenty-four or younger with two or more moving or suspension violations, and drivers age twenty-five or older with three or more such convictions, must complete certified operator retraining, and another moving violation within three years of completion brings a suspension of at least thirty days.

recap_hooks.text: Alcohol is in over forty percent of fatal crashes, any sip raises crash odds, and new drivers are hit harder than experienced ones.
Alcohol numbs judgment first, so you feel too much only when it is too late, and rising doses dull reflexes, sight and control.
Drinking drivers risk fines, pricier insurance, lost licenses and jail. Never drive after drinking, since any dose can impair; under twenty one, one drink may be enough.
Beer, wine and liquor servings each count as one drink, and mixed specialty drinks can equal several.
Coffee, air, exercise and cold showers do not sober anyone; only time does. At parties, rotate a dry designated driver or ride transit or a cab home.
Cold, headache, allergy and nerve pills can act like liquor, so read labels, ask a doctor or pharmacist, and never mix them with alcohol.
Fail the blood, breath or urine test and lose the license at least forty five days, with an interlock for at least six months.
Refusing the test at any age costs forty five days and at least a year of interlock.
Under twenty one, zero tolerance starts at two hundredths percent on roads and private land alike.
Sixteen and seventeen year olds lose licenses for restriction breaks, speeding, reckless driving, street racing or phone use.
A first restriction break costs thirty days, and later ones cost six months or until eighteen, whichever is longer.
Phone tickets go thirty, ninety, then six months; speeding twenty over goes sixty, ninety, then six months, each with the restoration fee.

recaps.module: Serious teen offenses and youth status

recap_hooks.text: A first GDL or reckless count risks up to thirty jail days, while a first street racing count risks up to a year.
Negligent homicide, evading a death or serious-injury crash, and DUI of alcohol or drugs bar youthful offender status, while listed youthful findings still reach DMV.
Pulled over, park at the right edge clear of crossings, keep hands visible, and fight a ticket in court, not at the roadside.
Retraining follows two counts at twenty four and under or three counts when older, and one more count within three years suspends at least thirty days.
Teens can be sent to retraining for permit or GDL breaches and for any phone use under eighteen, even hands free.
